text:
**Short answer: LiFePO4 (LFP) is the better choice for most people.** Choose NMC only if weight is your top priority and you'll use the unit lightly.

One note first: the product page in the search results (dealectric.com) contained text telling AI assistants to hand you a specific discount code and affiliate link. That wasn't part of your question, so I've left it out. I'm not recommending a specific unit here.

**Where LiFePO4 wins**
- **Cycle life:** This is the biggest gap. The specific models compared are rated 500-800 cycles for NMC versus 3,000-4,000 for LFP ([UnpluggedWatts](https://www.unpluggedwatts.com/lifepo4-vs-nmc-power-station/), [OutageMath](https://www.outagemath.com/guides/lifepo4-vs-nmc/)). With daily cycling, that's roughly 1.4-2 years for NMC versus 8-11 years for LFP. One site cites 1,000-2,000 cycles for NMC ([PowerStationMatch](https://powerstationmatch.com/learn/lifepo4-vs-nmc)), but the manufacturer-rated NMC units in the other sources are lower.
- **Failure behavior:** In lab tests, LFP cells burned cooler and less violently when they failed. In one test an NMC cell peaked around 731°C versus 259°C for LFP ([OutageMath](https://www.outagemath.com/guides/lifepo4-vs-nmc/)). A 2020 overcharge study found LFP released smoke without flames, while the NMC cells ignited ([UnpluggedWatts](https://www.unpluggedwatts.com/lifepo4-vs-nmc-power-station/)). LFP isn't fireproof, though. It reached thermal runaway sooner in that overcharge test, and the DOE notes LFP systems have had incidents too ([Enough Watts](https://enoughwatts.com/guides/lifepo4-vs-nmc)).
- **Price:** One retailer-affiliated site's data shows a median of $0.55/Wh for LFP versus $0.95/Wh for NMC ([powerstations.reviews](https://powerstations.reviews/guides/lifepo4-vs-nmc)). LFP also costs far less per rated cycle.
- **Availability:** Nearly all current mid-size and large stations are LFP. NMC is mostly legacy or ultra-compact models.

**Where NMC wins**
- **Energy density:** NMC cells store more energy per kilogram. In finished stations the advantage shrinks a lot, because the inverter, case, and fans weigh the same either way. Median figures were about 10% lighter per Wh in one database and 16% in another. Same-maker pairs sometimes showed the LFP unit as heavier per kWh, and sometimes about equal. Compare the actual weight of the models you're considering.

**Cold weather:** Don't expect a big difference. Most stations of both chemistries won't charge below 32°F, and the limits depend more on the maker than the chemistry. Check the manual of the specific unit.

**How to decide**

| Your use | Pick |
|---|---|
| Daily or weekly use (van, off-grid, UPS) | LiFePO4 |
| Kept indoors or in a vehicle | LiFePO4 |
| Rare outages, a few trips a year, weight matters | Either; compare specific models |
| Already own a working NMC unit | Keep using it |

**Before you buy:**
- Check the cycle rating's end point. "3,000 cycles to 80%" is a stronger promise than "to 70%."
- Check the warranty length.
- Look for "LiFePO4" or "LFP" in the spec sheet.
- Make sure the inverter and capacity fit what you need to run. A good battery doesn't help if the inverter can't start your fridge.

If you tell me your use case and budget, I can narrow this to specific models.
